reports.headline: Friday 6 November in Spain: “Les Misérables” in three hours, the Catalan horror “11” and a documentary on Carmen Laforet
reports.deck: Besides the big openings already covered, the Friday bill includes a faithful Hugo adaptation, a debut from two cousins in Sitges and a literary documentary.
paragraphs: Fred Cavayé's “Les Misérables” (“Los miserables”) opens in Spain today with Vincent Lindon as Jean Valjean and Tahar Rahim as Javert, plus Camille Cottin, Benjamin Lavernhe and Noémie Merlant. It runs close to three hours, according to Cinemascomics. After its San Sebastián screening, SensaCine's critic praised its fidelity to the novel and the cast, but thought that same fidelity is its limit: it finds no new way to tell the story, and the second half feels heavy. We haven't seen it; this is her view, not ours.

“11” is the first feature by cousins Paula and Clàudia Serra, who began it as a university script at Pompeu Fabra. Ara says it was the only film in original Catalan in the Sitges competition. A group of scouts is cut off by a snowstorm in a mountain refuge when an unexpected presence appears; the directors say they cared less about where the evil comes from than about the mistrust it causes. It lasts about 90 minutes. Ara singles out Mia Sala-Patau's performance. We have only read about it.

Also opening is “Por qué no escribo nada”, Isabel Fernández's documentary on novelist Carmen Laforet, with contributions from Najat El Hachmi and Laura Freixas; it won best music at the BCN Film Fest. The rest of the bill (“Godzilla Minus Zero”, “Sacamantecas”, “Ruega por nosotras”, “Fiesta Pagäna”) is in earlier editions.

reports.headline: Tallinn Black Nights opens its 30th edition today with 230 features, a Basque spotlight and new films by Zvyagintsev and McDonagh
reports.deck: The festival runs until 22 November in Tallinn and Tartu; the opening film is the Latvian-led Baltic co-production “Ulya”.
paragraphs: PÖFF, the Tallinn Black Nights festival, runs from 6 to 22 November. Its own programme lists 230 features and 259 shorts from 87 countries, with 107 world premieres. The opening film is “Ulya”, a co-production between Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania led by Latvia.

The programme names Andrey Zvyagintsev's “Minotaur”, Martin McDonagh's “Wild Horse Nine”, Paweł Pawlikowski's “Fatherland”, Peter Farrelly's “I Am Rocky” and “The Black Ball”, by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo. There is a spotlight on Basque cinema, and Max Korman's “Joy Will Prevail”, about architect Louis Kahn, has its international premiere on 7 November.

The documentary competitions run from 7 to 13 November; the Official Selection, First Feature, Rebels with a Cause, Critics' Picks and Baltic competitions run from 13 to 19. The jury and the full competition list were not on the pages we read, so we don't give them. We don't know which of these films will reach Spain.

reports.headline: Friday on the platforms in Spain: “Wuthering Heights” on Movistar Plus+, “Palacio” and “Un amor posible” on Netflix, and Filmin's batch
reports.deck: A platform guide lists the 6 November releases; we only confirmed the title and platform, not the details of each work.
paragraphs: MarketingDirecto's guide for 6-15 November puts on Netflix the film “Un amor posible”, the series “Palacio” and the documentary “Desprotexida: El crimen de Pazos”. On Movistar Plus+ comes “Wuthering Heights” (“Cumbres borrascosas”) and the third season of the documentary series “Una vida en diez fotos”. Prime Video adds the series “Campus Drivers” and HBO Max “Melania Rea”.

Filmin lists “Eleonora Duse, la divina”, “En la alcoba del sultán”, “Broken English”, “La vida era eso” and “Barrio triste”. “Duse” and “Barrio triste” were covered yesterday. For the next days the same guide mentions “Carmen Curlers” season three on Filmin on the 10th and “La copia perfecta” on the 13th. A single source: dates may change.

reports.headline: OperaVision lists Andriessen's “De Materie” from Opera Ballet Vlaanderen for tonight at 19:00 CET
reports.deck: It is a scheduled broadcast; we have not verified a complete recording with stated access, so we don't file it as one.
paragraphs: OperaVision's home page puts “De Materie”, by Louis Andriessen, in its “coming soon” list for 6 November at 19:00 CET, from Opera Ballet Vlaanderen. The company's page describes a new production directed by Phia Ménard, conducted by Bas Wiegers, lasting about 1 hour 50 minutes. The OperaVision page does not state subtitles or how long it will stay online.

The same list gives “Šárka” (Janáček, National Theatre Brno) on 15 November, “Little Bear and the Ice Mountain” and “Turandot. Riddles at the museum” on 22 November, and Britten's “Peter Grimes” (Finnish National Opera and Ballet) on 26 November. “Le Roi d'Ys” is still marked “last chance to watch”. We found no new verified complete theatre recording today.

reports.headline: Calendar: Tallinn from today, Kahn's biopic on the 7th, “Carmen” in cinemas on the 10th and “El cuerpo” on the 11th
reports.deck: Dates checked today, each with its territory; Spanish cinema openings of the 6th are in the first report and in yesterday's edition.
paragraphs: Friday 6: Tallinn Black Nights opens (Estonia); “De Materie” on OperaVision at 19:00 CET; platform releases in Spain as above. Saturday 7: international premiere of “Joy Will Prevail” in Tallinn; documentary competitions until the 13th. Sunday 8: season two of “City of God: The Fight Rages On” on HBO Max in Spain, and “Le Roi d'Ys” is still marked as last chance.

Tuesday 10: the Royal Ballet and Opera's “Carmen” in cinemas (international; Spain unconfirmed). Wednesday 11: “El cuerpo” and “Avedon” on Netflix. Friday 13: “La copia perfecta” on Filmin; Tallinn's competitions begin. Sunday 15: “Šárka” on OperaVision. Sunday 22: Tallinn closes. Thursday 26: “Peter Grimes” on OperaVision. Dates come from the cited guides and may change.

reports.subject: film
reports.headline: Editor's picks: “Les Misérables” if you like the classics, “11” for Catalan horror, and Tallinn's “Joy Will Prevail”
reports.deck: Editorial affinity, not a critics' or audience score.
paragraphs: “Les Misérables” (cinemas in Spain, 6 November). Affinity 3 out of 5, medium confidence: a period drama with a strong cast, but the critic we cite warns of a heavy second half. We haven't seen it.

“11” (cinemas in Spain, 6 November). Affinity 4 out of 5, low confidence: folk-like mountain horror from two debut directors, judged only from an interview and synopses. “Joy Will Prevail” (Tallinn, international premiere on 7 November): affinity 3 out of 5, low confidence, since we only know its subject, the architect Louis Kahn; it has no date in Spain.

The day in brief: a Friday of period drama and Catalan horror in cinemas, a new festival starting in the Baltics and an opera from Belgium tonight. No physical-media or industry news was verified today.
